visuals.heading: The Real Roles Inside a Science Museum

rows: The core scientific-content role: researching topics, writing exhibit text, verifying scientific accuracy, and often leading a subject gallery or department inside a centre. Usually needs a first-class M.Sc. (or B.E./B.Tech for technology-focused centres) plus a demonstrated ability to explain science simply.

Designs and builds the physical and interactive exhibits people walk through, working with fabricators, electronics teams, and designers to turn a scientific concept into something a visitor can touch and understand in under a minute.

Runs the visitor-facing programme: guided tours, science demonstrations, school workshops, science shows, and the planetarium sky-shows where a centre has a planetarium. This is the role closest to what most people picture when they hear "science communicator."
Maintains and operates exhibits, planetarium projection systems, and lab equipment. A real, steady technical track, usually reachable with a diploma or B.Sc rather than a postgraduate degree.
